definitions.text: nflverse public release assets, regular season only: the weekly injury reports (injuries_<season>.csv: one row per player per team per game week, the week's final report, with its game status and the last practice day's participation), the weekly rosters (roster_weekly_<season>.csv: each player's status that game week), PFR snap counts (snap_counts_<season>.csv: every player who took at least one snap) and the schedule (games.csv). 2025 is never read (held out, calibration.md §7).

A team game is one team's side of one regular-season game. A team interval is a team game followed by another team game of the same regular season (so each team-season has games − 1): a new injury shows up as the next game missed, so it can only be seen in an interval. A team's final regular-season game is exposure no injury can be seen after, and is left out of both the counts and the denominators.

Took at least one snap (offence, defence or special teams) in the game, from the snap counts. The weekly roster's ACT/INA split is not used for this: it is not reliable for the game itself (2019 lists injured, unused players as ACT).

Did not play, and either was on injured reserve (R01, R48, or a RES row with no code in 2019 and early 2020), PUP (R04, R47, PUP) or the non-football list (R05, R49, RSN), or was on the 53 and on the final injury report with an injury (not 'not injury related', rest, personal, coach's decision or COVID) and a game designation (Questionable, Doubtful, Out) or a practice limit (did not participate, limited). Illness counts, as its own class. COVID lists, suspensions, the practice squad and holdouts never count. The weekly roster can lag a reserve move by a week (Dak Prescott, DAL 2020 w6), so a game with no snap and no report line between a game he played and a reserve-list game counts as missed for that injury.

A run of one or more consecutive team games missed for injury. It is new in season when, the team game before it, he played (onset AFTER_PLAYED: hurt in that game, that week's practice or away from football) or was healthy on the 53 and did not play (AFTER_NOT_PLAYED: hurt in practice or away). Spells already running at the team's first game (BEFORE_SEASON) and spells whose game before is unclear (not on the 53, or listed hurt without playing) are counted apart and left out of the new-injury rates. The headline counts football injuries; illness and the non-football list are reported beside them.

Games missed: consecutive team games missed (byes skipped). Weeks out: calendar weeks from the first missed game's week to the week of the game he was back for (byes count), which is ADR-087's weeksRemaining. A spell ends when he plays, or is healthy on the 53 without playing; it is censored when the regular season ends or he leaves the team's list (cut, traded, practice squad, COVID list).

ADR-087 §5.3: SHORT 1-3, LONG 4-8, MAJOR 9 or more, in games (and, beside it, in weeks). Shares come from a Kaplan-Meier survival curve over the new in-season spells, so a censored spell counts only for as long as it was seen (a censored length c says D ≥ c). 'Naive' shares treat censored lengths as exact and are a floor on the long bands.

An episode is a run of consecutive team game weeks on the injury list: missed for a football injury, or on the report with a football injury and a designation or practice limit. A new in-season episode has an AFTER_PLAYED or AFTER_NOT_PLAYED onset. A day-to-day injury is a new designated episode (a game designation or a missed game at some point) that never cost a game. 'Any' episodes also count practice-limit-only listings.

Per team-game: new in-season time-loss injuries / team intervals. Per player-game (by group): the group's new in-season injuries / the group's player-games played that had a next team game. Per 1, 000 snaps (by group): new injuries after a game he played / snaps in those player-games.

From the weekly roster's position (its most common value for the player on that team that season): QB; RB (incl. FB); WR; TE; OL; DL (DE, DT, NT); LB (incl. OLB, so 3-4 edge rushers are LB and 4-3 ends DL); DB; K/P (K, P, LS).

The report's injury text, read into a class by keyword (the earliest-named part wins; 'left'/'right' ignored): from the first missed game's report, else the week before, else any week of the spell, else the two weeks after it (players placed straight on IR are not on the report until they return). 'unknown' when none of those weeks has one.

From the weekly rosters: in season, a team game week 2..N on injured reserve after a week not on IR, PUP or NFI (list transfers are not new placements; an activation followed by a second placement counts twice); before week 1, on IR at the team's first game.

limits: The report names a body part, never a diagnosis: 'Knee' is an ACL tear and a bruise alike, so kinds such as ACL, MCL or a high ankle sprain cannot be counted.
Only the week's final report is published per player: a player limited on Wednesday and full on Friday shows as full; earlier days are not seen.

Healthy scratches: an inactive player who is not on the report reads as a healthy scratch. A hurt player his team left off the report reads healthy, and a healthy scratch listed with a designation or a practice limit reads as missed for injury.

Players placed straight onto IR after a game are never on that week's report, so their body part comes from their return weeks or is unknown (about 11% of spells, skewed to the longest injuries: their MAJOR share is about 75%). The body-part shares therefore understate the serious kinds.

Injury reserve rules shape the games-missed numbers: in 2019 IR was season-ending except two designated returns a team (8 weeks minimum); 2020-2021 had a 3-week minimum; 2022 on, 4 games. Teams also shut injured players down late in a lost season. Recorded games missed therefore overstate medical time lost for some players, and inflate LONG and MAJOR, most of all in 2019.

Kaplan-Meier assumes censoring is unrelated to how bad an injury is. Censoring here is the season's end (unrelated) or the player leaving the team's list (a team cutting an injured player with an injury settlement is related, and rare).

Injuries in a team's last regular-season game, in the playoffs and in the offseason are not seen; a week-1 absence is called carried over only when the player ended the previous regular season out injured.
Practice and game injuries cannot be told apart for a player who played the game before: the reports say who is hurt, not where. The practice numbers below are hints, each with its own assumptions.

Snap counts meet the roster by PFR id and, for the roster rows with no PFR id (about a third), by normalised name within the team-week; about 1% of snap rows meet no roster row (see Coverage) and a listed player whose snap row was lost reads as having missed the game.

2020 and 2021: the COVID-19 lists (R59, RSR) and 2020's opt-outs (R62, NWT) are not injuries and never count; 2020's moved games and 2022's cancelled BUF-CIN game follow the schedule. 2019 and 2020 to week 7 carry no reserve codes, so every RES row there is read as IR (a few reserve players of other kinds are in it).
The practice squad is left out: a practice-squad player hurt in practice misses no game of the 53.
'Players missing 4+ games' counts what was seen: an injury late in the season cannot reach 4 games before the season ends.
